questions.q: What did Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 5 already establish, according to this lesson?
options: The six Run if conditions
Databricks Asset Bundle YAML syntax
The shared-vs-separate job cluster decision inside a multi-task job
The basic split: all-purpose clusters cost more per DBU than job clusters, which have no idle risk
questions.explain: Lesson 5 covered the basic all-purpose-vs-job-cluster cost distinction; this lesson goes one level deeper into multi-task jobs specifically.

questions.q: In a job using one shared job cluster, how many clusters does the job provision?
options: One per task, always
As many as there are dependencies
Zero — shared clusters use no compute
One — used by every task in the job
questions.explain: A shared job cluster is provisioned once and used by every task, the cheapest and simplest option.

questions.q: What is the real benefit of giving each task its own separate job cluster?
options: It is always cheaper than a shared cluster
It removes the need for Run if conditions
Isolation — each task's compute is sized independently, and one task's configuration doesn't constrain another's
It eliminates the need for a trigger
questions.explain: Separate clusters cost more in aggregate but buy real isolation between tasks with very different compute needs.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when is a shared job cluster the right choice?
options: Never — separate clusters are always preferred
When every task has similar, modest compute needs
Only when the job has exactly one task
Only for jobs using a file-arrival trigger
questions.explain: Sharing one cluster makes sense when tasks don't have very different sizing needs, minimizing total job cost.

questions.q: Is 'job cluster is cheaper than all-purpose cluster' still true whether tasks share a cluster or use separate ones?
options: No — separate job clusters are always billed as all-purpose clusters
The distinction no longer applies once a job has more than one task
No — shared job clusters are billed as all-purpose clusters
Yes — that basic distinction from Lesson 5 holds regardless of the shared-vs-separate choice
questions.explain: Lesson 5's job-vs-all-purpose cost distinction remains true; shared-vs-separate is a separate decision layered on top of it.
